content.title: Where is Siena University? Location, history, and facts about the March Madness underdog
content.text: Where exactly is this "Cinderella" school located?Siena UniversityEvery March, a small school captures the heart of the nation by crashing the Big Dance. In 2026, that team is the Siena Saints. While college basketball fans are familiar with the "Green and Gold" jerseys and their tenacious defense, many are heading to Google to locate the campus. If you are wondering where Siena University is and what makes this institution unique, here is everything you need to know.To watch this video, agree to share video information with third partiesAgree|More infoThe Heart of the Capital RegionSiena College (often referred to as Siena University in casual search) is located in Loudonville, New York. Loudonville is an affluent suburban community in the Town of Colonie, situated just a few miles north of Albany, the state capital.Así juega Robbie Avila, el antihéroe del March Madness que podría jugar con MéxicoIts strategic location in the Hudson Valley puts the campus in a prime geographic spot:Distance to Albany: 10 minutes.Distance to New York City: Approximately 2.5 hours north.Distance to Boston: Approximately 3 hours west.A Franciscan TraditionFounded in 1937, Siena is a private Catholic liberal arts college rooted in the Franciscan tradition. The school was named after Saint Bernardino of Siena, a 15th-century Italian preacher. This heritage is reflected in the campus's "Saints" nickname and its commitment to community service and social justice. Despite its relatively small undergraduate enrollment (roughly 3,000 to 3,500 students), the school punches far above its weight class in both academics and athletics.The MVP Arena: Home of the SaintsWhile the campus is in Loudonville, the basketball team plays its home games at the MVP Arena in downtown Albany. This creates a unique "big-city" atmosphere for a mid-major program, often drawing crowds that rival those of much larger universities. This strong local support is a major reason why Siena has remained a powerhouse in the Metro Atlantic Athletic Conference (MAAC) for decades.March Madness - EnglishNCAAM - English
